t: This is the corner of Wardour Street and Peter Street in Soho, where the Intrepid Fox pub once stood at numbers 97 to 99. It's a former public house now. It was established in 1784 by the publican Samuel House, who named it after Charles James Fox, the Whig statesman. Fox sat in Parliament for thirty-eight years, and he was the great rival of the Tory William Pitt the Younger. His father, Henry Fox, had been a leading Whig and the rival of Pitt's father too.
